thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for service `inference-queue-service` -> Escalation level: P1. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/P12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Alert details: metric=queue_depth, value=2187, threshold=600 (5m avg). Cluster=prod-us-west-2, pool=inference-shared. Autoscaler observed 96% node utilization and failed scale attempts: 3.

maria (oncall): ack - I'm on it, reassigning. Investigating autoscaler logs and k8s events.

devon: I can help — looking at cloud provider quota and recent spot failures. if needed we can force-add nodes.

josh: seeing elevated 50x KV cache miss rate on the hot prefix, kvcache warmup looks stalled. That explains token regen + long tails.

samir: confirming client impact: ~12% of requests getting 5xx (502/504) and median latency for generation up from 120ms -> 1.8s. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.

maria (oncall): ok plan: 1) temporary manual scale to relieve queue 2) disable aggressive batching on the busiest route 3) kick kvcache warmup job 4) update statuspage.

devon: manual scale now: `kubectl scale deployment inference-worker --replicas=30 -n prod` (running from bastion).

ops-bot: Command output: `deployment.apps/inference-worker scaled`

josh: hitting the dataservice: kvcache process shows `warmup_progress: 27%` and many `kvcache_fetch` timeouts. Starting a restart of the kvcache migrator job.

maria (oncall): restarting migrator: ```kubectl rollout restart job/kvcache-warmup -n prod && kubectl logs -f job/kvcache-warmup -n prod```

devon: cloud quota looked fine but a flurry of spot termination events in the last 10m caused nodes to drop and the autoscaler to oscillate. I've opened a request to increase diversity of instance pools.

pagerduty-bot: If alert not acknowledged in 5m, will escalate to SRE lead.

product-ops: heads-up — we have a small enterprise customer noticing degraded throughput (they're on Dedicated but routing fallback to Hosted). Status page should reflect partial degradation for hosted inference.

statuspage-bot: Statuspage update: "Investigating - Performance degradation for hosted inference (some requests failing/slow)." link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-789

samir: manual scale is helping — queue dropped from 2187 -> 900 in 6m. 5xx rate down to ~7%. Keep an eye on warmup job.

josh: warmup job logs show steady progress now, missing keys being seeded. Also disabled `auto-batch=aggressive` on route `/v1/embeddings` to reduce per-request queueing. Config change: `route.config.embeddings.batch_policy=conservative` (deployed).

maria (oncall): autoscaler still unstable: controller logs show `scale attempt failed: insufficient capacity` and `throttled by cloud provider`. I'm going to flip a temporary fallback policy to route lower-tier traffic to a cheaper model variant to reduce pressure. Applying routing policy: ```redwoodctl routing set-fallback --route /v1/generate --variant small-compat --duration 10m```

devon: applied. Observed immediate drop in token generation pressure, queue now ~420.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PAGER acknowledged by maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): summary so far in-thread for handoff: cause = kvcache warmup stalls + spot node churn -> autoscaler couldn't replenish capacity fast enough -> queue buildup -> customer-visible 5xx/latency. Mitigation = manual scale, restart warmup job, conservative batching, routing fallback.

josh: I'll follow up post-incident to add a kvcache warmup health check and make warmup job idempotent for quicker retries.

devon: I'll file a ticket to widen instance pool mix and add a quota buffer so autoscaler has spare capacity.

maria (oncall): preparing the short incident note for the on-call rotation and ops roster: taking this to an ops-handoff in 20m unless resolved. Who wants ownership for retrospective?

samir: I'll own the retrospective and the followup.

product-ops: customers to notify: list from routing logs shows 14 customers with >0.5% errors in last 10m. Recommend email to those above 1% with summary and expected follow-up.

statuspage-bot: Updated: "Identified - root cause appears to be cache warmup + capacity churn; mitigations applied. Partial service degradation continues but improving."

maria (oncall): last checks — queue 210, 5xx ~2.1%, median latency 350ms. Leaving a watcher on until autoscaler stabilizes. Handing to night oncall in 25m if no regression.

incident-bot: Note added: `runbook: autoscaler-queue-backlog` recommended, postmortem owner: samir.

maria (oncall): handoff: tagging @night-oncall. Please watch the autoscaler controller for spikes: `kubectl get events -n prod | grep autoscaler` and check `metrics.autoscaler.scale_attempts` in grafana.

night-oncall: ack - will monitor.

samir: followups: create kvcache warmup alert (warmup_time > 3m), add autoscaler spike guard (prevent oscillation on repeated spot terminations), update runbook with manual scale commands and fallback routing steps.

maria (oncall): thanks team. filing the incident ticket: INC-2026-PD-P12345. Closing the PD escalation once postmortem plan set. :white_check_mark:
